items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mingus was with the band then. Mingus is sitting on the left side of the bus, two seats behind me.

ctx.x: Another incident I came across related to Duke’s band was an incident involving Tony Scott and Charles Mingus.

Oh yeah. Charles Mingus – Tony, rather, always wanted to play in Ellington’s band, and he always wanted to play Ben Webster’s book in Ellington’s band. So we finally got that going. The first trip was down South. We traveled on the bus. Mingus is sitting – Mingus was with the band then. Mingus is sitting on the left side of the bus, two seats behind me. I’m sitting about two seat up on the right side. In front of me is . . .

items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: I asked Duke, when are we going to make that record, Clark Terry, Dan Jones, myself and you and some you want, to make a real avant garde record?

ctx.x: What are some of the other -- that's interesting, about being able to play in and out, and being an actor. Who are some of the people most able to do that? You mentioned Bird and --
I have to tell you about what Duke has done. Like, I asked Duke, when are we going to make that record, Clark Terry, Dan Jones, myself and you and some you want, to make a real avant garde record?
